title: Grilling Summary

short.lead: The grilling session for the #306 restructure is done: round 5 raised no new question. This page gathers every answer from the five rounds into ten topics, so you can confirm them in one place. Each topic names the round and answer each decision comes from. The full wording of each round is in the decisions log (docs/6-decisions/Decisions.md): rounds 1 and 2 on the branch AjsAgent/docs-context-layer, rounds 3 to 5 on AjsAgent/issue-281-fix. Once you confirm, I will write the build plan for the restructure from these answers.
short.hint: Tap a topic to see every answer it holds.
items: Deleting a file that git can restore is always allowed on a branch the agent owns. On anyone else's branch it is refused, and the refusal gives the reason (round 1, answer 1). Risky git commands are refused with the safe way named, and you are asked only when no safe way exists (round 1, answer 2). A branch is the agent's own when its name starts with the agent prefix or an extra prefix in the settings (round 2, answer 5). A snapshot branch (the autosave copy of a helper's worktree) is deleted once that helper's work is merged (round 2, answer 7).
Round 1 answers 1 and 2; round 2 answers 5 and 7.

Test suites are run twice, by the main session and by helper agents alike (round 1, answer 3). The agent never skips a check itself. When a check takes over 10 minutes, costs money, or needs a machine or account the agent can't reach, the agent names the check and asks you plainly. Skipping a test or hiding a failure is only ever your decision (round 2, answer 12, your own wording). The agent uses Unity batch mode to check that a project compiles only when no Unity command-line tool or editor plugin can (round 1, answer 15).

A helper with a question only you can answer stops and reports it to the parent session, which asks you (round 1, answer 4). A helper's report quotes the real RESULT line and every failure line, with no line limit (round 1, answer 5). Worktree autosave credits its commits the same way as every other commit, and pushes to a new snapshot branch each time without force-pushing (round 1, answer 12). The worktree sweep commits a finished helper's uncommitted leftovers, and only inside that helper's own worktree (round 1, answer 13).

An obvious bug outside the request is not fixed unasked; it becomes an issue named in the reply (round 1, answer 6). Every feature that reaches a build plan gets GitHub issues (round 1, answer 8). A feature that is one step of a bigger one passes QA on its own, and its parent closes with the last child (round 1, answer 9). The parent is found through GitHub's sub-issue link (round 2, answer 8). An approval is accepted before its decisions-log entry exists, and the work can't move on until that entry is written (round 1, answer 10). The design loop's stage moves through pull requests and labels stay as written rules, and trying to edit code never moves a stage (round 1, answer 11).
Where pages are built and how you read them

In local sessions, pages are built on your machine for every plan and long reply, and published to claude.ai only when you ask (round 1, answer 7). In cloud sessions, where tapping a page's HTML file shows raw code instead of the rendered page, every page is published privately to claude.ai and the reply links it. The page file is still written under docs/plans/ and committed to git (round 5, answer 1C).
The agent's name, credit and branches

Identity and taste become settings that you choose. Safety and evidence rules stay fixed, enforced as refusals. "Claude" is never the default credit, and neither is your name on someone else's work (round 1, answer 16, your own wording). The agent's name is the GitHub login, lowercased, plus "sAgent": ajw2003sAgent for you (round 2, answer 1). That name is the commit author's name, with your own email address (round 2, answer 2). The credit line reads "Committed by ajw2003sAgent" on commits and "Opened by ajw2003sAgent" on pull requests and issues (round 2, answer 3). Agent branches are named ajw2003sAgent/<topic> (round 2, answer 4). AjsAgent/ and claude/ stay in your settings as extra agent prefixes, and nothing is renamed (round 2, answer 6).
Round 1 answer 16; round 2 answers 1 to 4 and 6.
How settings are asked for and kept

Every setting must be set before work can start; none falls back to an assumed default (round 2, answer 13). At session start the plugin asks for each unset setting in the chat and suggests the worked-out value, which is used only once you confirm it. A value you set through the /plugin configure command is accepted too (round 3, answer 1A). Until the settings are set, every tool is refused, and the refusal names the missing setting (round 3, answer 2B). The one command allowed meanwhile is the plugin's own settings script (round 4, answer 1A). Cloud sessions read settings from environment variables set once in the cloud environment's settings, then from the settings file (round 4, answer 2A).
Round 2 answer 13; round 3 answers 1A and 2B; round 4 answers 1A and 2A.

The archivist moves a long code comment into the docs at turn end and leaves a doc-ref pointer, a one-line marker naming where the text went (round 1, answer 14). On someone else's branch it opens an issue instead of moving the comment (round 2, answer 9). In a repo you don't own, the six-tier docs under docs/ stay on your machine and out of git, unless the owner asks for them (round 2, answer 10).
What counts as a wholesale rewrite
A wholesale rewrite is replacing more than half of a file's lines in one change, or writing the whole file over, and it needs your approval by name (round 2, answer 11).
You accepted the sixteen mechanical fixes exactly as listed on the round 1 page (docs/plans/2026-10-18-grilling-round-1.html) (round 1, answer 17).
